days.why: A red-eye day gets one real sight (Temple of Heaven, whose halls open exactly when you arrive) plus its neighbour Qianmen, then a hotel break, then two low-effort evening strolls — Wangfujing is 400 m from the door and Shichahai is the dusk payoff. Beijing city model added beside Qianmen — free, indoor and a useful orientation before the imperial core on d2.

Everything sits inside one 3 km square and the order is dictated by timed entry. The two meals are deliberately off-convention and they are what make the day work: a 06:30 breakfast buys the National Museum its afternoon back (the museum shuts at 17:00, and on a 07:00 start the chain only reached it at 14:54 — barely 2 h of a 3 h visit), and a 17:00 dinner, eaten as the museum closes, is what puts you on Jingshan at 19:06 with sunset at 19:22. Order: square from 07:42, Forbidden City on the 08:30 morning slot, museum through the worst of the heat in air conditioning, then dinner, then the climb for the golden-roof panorama.

days.theme: Great Wall, then the CBD lit up
days.why: Walk the wall before the heat and luge straight down it (the toboggan is the descent, not a separate trip — it shuts at 17:00), eat at Mutianyu, then let the 90-minute drive back down the north-east corridor deliver you into Sanlitun. Dinner is pulled to 17:30 so it lands as Taikoo Li closes out and CCTV moves to 19:31 — past the 19:19 sunset, which is the only time that stop is worth making. CCTV now takes the full hour its research allows rather than the 30-minute minimum: it is the lit tower, plus the free China World Mall terrace.

One long north-west morning at the Summer Palace from opening, then a single cross-town hop east to the 798 compound, with UCCA saved for last because it stays open to 19:00 when the smaller galleries have already shut. Lunch is pulled to 11:30 so it lands as the Summer Palace ends: on the default noon window it slid all the way past the 798 drive to 15:13, which is eight hours after breakfast.

Check-in at Daxing is 07:40 for the 09:40 to Lijiang, and Daxing is 55 km south — a 68-minute run, to an airport you have never used and did not fly into. On the default window breakfast started 05:49 and the chain reached check-in at exactly 07:40, i.e. zero margin against a booked flight. Breakfast at 05:30 puts you at PKX around 07:21 with ~20 minutes in hand. Order the car and a breakfast box the night before; nothing will be open.

ideas.name: Mutianyu night tour
ideas.why: It is an either/or with the daytime wall, not an add-on: doing both means either dead-waiting 8 hours on site or a second 140 km round trip, and it would cost you the whole Sanlitun/CBD evening.

notes: Aug 11–15 2026 is Tue–Sat, so no Monday closures bite: the Forbidden City, National Museum, UCCA and the Planning Hall are all open on the days they are scheduled.

Forbidden City (12 Aug): from 2026 there are no gate sales at all. Tickets release 7 days ahead — book at 20:00 Beijing time on 5 Aug, via the Palace Museum site or WeChat mini-program, passport details exact. Take the MORNING slot (entry 08:30–12:00); peak-season slots sell out in minutes.
Tiananmen Square needs its own separate free reservation, also 7 days ahead — book it in the same sitting as the Forbidden City. Plan to clear security ~07:30.

National Museum (12 Aug): free but reservation is mandatory, released 7 days ahead at 17:00 Beijing time. The whole afternoon depends on getting the 13:30 slot (summer third slot runs 13:30–16:30; the museum closes 17:00, last admission 16:00).

Temple of Heaven: the park gates open 06:00 but the halls only open 08:00 — do not go straight from the airport, take the bag drop and breakfast first and arrive about 08:00. Enter by the quieter North Gate; joint ticket.

Mutianyu: the toboggan and chairlift run 08:00–17:00 (cable car 07:30–17:30), so the luge has to happen on the morning visit — it cannot slide to the end of the day. Leave the hotel 06:30–07:00 by private driver, ~1.5 h each way. Note: from June 2026 visitors over 60 may be refused the toboggan.

The Mutianyu night tour IS running on 13 Aug (season 25 Jun–31 Aug, but suspended 13 Jul–10 Aug, so you just miss the blackout). Wall lighting ~19:30–21:00, night check-in 17:30–20:30, cable car to 21:00. If you would rather have the illuminated wall than the CBD, swap the whole of day 3 to an afternoon departure — but you lose Sanlitun and CCTV and get back near midnight.

Summer Palace: gates 06:00, buildings 08:00. Start at the North Palace Gate at opening, do Longevity Hill, then take the lake ferry across and exit east — that puts you on the right side of the city for the run over to 798.
UCCA and most of 798 close around 18:00–19:00, so day 4 does not tolerate a slow Summer Palace morning; if you are running late, cut the 798 wander rather than UCCA.
Day 1 has a hard floor of ~06:30 at PEK plus ~60 min into town, and Regent check-in is not until 15:00 — the morning stop is a bell-desk bag drop only.

Day 5: PKX is Daxing, 46 km south of the centre, ~68 min. With the 120-min buffer against a 07:40 flight you are leaving the hotel around 04:15 — arrange a car the night before and a breakfast box, as nothing will be open.
